about: Fixed-partition Clifford width census. For each code and width w, EVERY partition of the qubits into cells of size <= w was solved to Completeness.COMPLETE and the best logical image recorded. 'exhaustive' rows carry unknown = 0, so 'short' is a certified negative for the ansatz, not a sampling artefact. Produced 2026-08-21/22 by memory/2026-08-21-width/ (staircase2.py, ct_shard.py, shard.py, stacked.py); decomposability by decomp.py.

reference.chakraborty_gottesman: arXiv:2602.13395, Theorem 1: implementing the full Clifford group on k logical qubits needs at least k-fold transversal gadgets, i.e. a fixed partition of width >= k. Their tightness example is k blocks of the [[7,1,3]] code.
reference.definition: A gadget set is w-fold transversal if ONE partition {s_i} with |s_i| <= w serves every gadget in the set.

rows.note: Chakraborty-Gottesman's own tightness example, reproduced here: cells are corresponding qubits of the two blocks.

staircases.note: The width-4 row has 12 partitions still unknown, which does not weaken the verdict: a FULL result needs one witness, and the width-3 negative below it is exhaustive.

phi_index.about: The symplectic cut |G| = |A^x| / |orbit of 1| under the congruence action a.u = sigma(u) a u, which replaced a sweep of A^x. All three rows returned UNKNOWN before it existed.

cross_validation.note: every width <= 2 partition of those four codes on which the sweep also terminates; both the physical order and the logical image agreed
